newsitem.title: USA: Morrison Knudsen moves in right direction - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Knudsen moves in right direction - Barron's.

text.p: Following its merger with Washington Construction Group and a two month bankruptcy this summer, Morrison Knudsen is now moving in the right direction, a Barron's report said.

Some investors expects Morrison Knudsen's stock to jump about 35 percent from its current level to $12 over the next year. Others expect the stock to nearly double to $15 by early 1998, Barron's said.
Morrison Knudsen's stock closed Friday at $9 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Barron's report said Morrison Knudsen's profits are "virtually guaranteed" to be at least $11 million this year.

In bankruptcy documents, Morrison Knudsen said it expects to have earnings of about $31 million or $0.59 a share in 1997 on revenues of $1.6 billion. In 1998, the company projected earnings of $37 million or $0.69 a share on revenues of $1.8 billion, Barron's said.
The company told Barron's that it has in its backlog between 70 percent and 80 percent of the work needed to meet those projections.

Morrison Knudsen also expects to expand its international presence. The company expected overseas projects to generate about 30 percent of revenues by the end of the century, up from about 15 percent currently, Barron's said.
The comapny also expects to boost its future returns by taking more equity positions in the projects it builds.
